descripcion_es: Phrases for giving an opinion, showing agreement or disagreement and responding politely.
resumen: Expressions for giving your point of view, asking for other people's, showing full or partial agreement and disagreeing without sounding abrupt; useful in debates and presentations.

explicacion.texto: In English “to agree” is a verb: I agree, not “I am agree” (Spanish says “estar de acuerdo”). In a formal debate disagreement is softened: instead of You're wrong, people say I'm not sure I agree or I see your point, but…

filas: In my opinion, …
Giving an opinion (es: en mi opinión)
In my opinion, the tax is unfair.
I think / believe / feel (that)…
Giving an opinion (es: creo / considero que)
I believe education is the key.
As far as I'm concerned, …
Giving an opinion (es: en lo que a mí respecta)
As far as I'm concerned, it's a waste of money.
From my point of view, …
Giving an opinion (es: desde mi punto de vista)
From my point of view, it's too risky.
It seems to me that…
Giving an opinion (es: me parece que)
It seems to me that prices will keep rising.
What do you think about…?
Asking for an opinion (es: ¿qué opinas de…?)
What do you think about remote work?
How do you feel about…?
Asking for an opinion (es: ¿qué te parece…?)
How do you feel about the new law?
What's your view on…?
Asking for an opinion, formal (es: ¿cuál es su postura sobre…?)
What's your view on nuclear energy?
I agree (with you).
Agreement (es: estoy de acuerdo)
I agree with you completely.
Absolutely! / Exactly!
Full agreement (es: ¡totalmente! / ¡exacto!)
Exactly! That's what I meant.
That's a good point.
Agreement (es: buena observación)
That's a good point; I hadn't thought of it.
I couldn't agree more.
Full agreement (es: no podría estar más de acuerdo)
I couldn't agree more.
I agree up to a point, but…
Partial agreement (es: hasta cierto punto)
I agree up to a point, but it's expensive.
I see what you mean, but…
Partial agreement (es: entiendo lo que dices, pero)
I see what you mean, but it won't work.
I'm not sure about that.
Mild disagreement (es: no estoy seguro)
I'm not sure about that, actually.
I'm afraid I disagree.
Polite disagreement (es: me temo que discrepo)
I'm afraid I disagree with the minister.
I don't agree (with…).
Disagreement (es: no estoy de acuerdo)
I don't agree with that idea.
That's not the point.
Countering (es: esa no es la cuestión)
That's not the point; the problem is the cost.
On the contrary, …
Countering (es: al contrario)
On the contrary, it will create jobs.
It depends.
Qualifying (es: depende)
It depends on the situation.

items: Agree with someone / with an idea; agree on a decision; agree to a proposal.
On the contrary rejects what has been said; to contrast two of your own ideas, use on the other hand.
Discuss means to talk about a subject (discuss a topic, without about); Spanish “discutir” in the sense of quarrelling is argue.

ejemplos.frase: As far as I'm concerned, public transport should be free for students.
ejemplos.traduccion: En lo que a mí respecta, el transporte público debería ser gratuito para los estudiantes.

ejemplos.frase: I agree with you up to a point, but the plan is too expensive.
ejemplos.traduccion: Estoy de acuerdo contigo hasta cierto punto, pero el plan es demasiado caro.

ejemplos.frase: I'm afraid I disagree: the figures don't support that conclusion.
ejemplos.traduccion: Me temo que discrepo: las cifras no respaldan esa conclusión.

ejemplos.frase: How do you feel about working at weekends?
ejemplos.traduccion: ¿Qué te parece trabajar los fines de semana?

ejemplos.frase: We discussed the proposal for two hours but didn't agree on anything.
ejemplos.traduccion: Debatimos la propuesta durante dos horas pero no nos pusimos de acuerdo en nada.

ejemplos.frase: That's a good point. I hadn't looked at it that way.
ejemplos.traduccion: Buena observación. No lo había visto de esa manera.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Agree is a verb; it does not take be.
Quarrelling is argue; discuss means to talk about a subject.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: According to me, it's a mistake.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: In my opinion, it's a mistake.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: According to is used for other sources, not for yourself.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card points out that we say agree with someone or with an idea. The clue is you: you agree with a person, and for that the preposition is with. The adverb completely reinforces the agreement and goes before the verb. Remember that agree does not take be.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To agree with someone is agree with.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Agree to is used with a proposal (agree to a plan), not with a person.
Agree on is used for reaching agreement on a decision, not with a person.
Agree about exists for the topic, but with the person we say agree with.

glosario.definicion_l: to a complete degree or to the full or entire extent; Completely or entirely · so as to be complete; with everything necessary

ejercicios.frase: As far as I'm ___, the meeting was a waste of time.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “As far as I'm concerned” (es: “en lo que a mí respecta”). The clue is the structure “As far as I'm ___”, a fixed phrase completed with the participle concerned. It is used to give a personal opinion with some emphasis. Do not confuse it with “as far as I know” (es: “que yo sepa”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “en lo que a mí respecta” is as far as I'm concerned.
ejercicios.traduccion: En lo que a mí respecta, la reunión fue una pérdida de tiempo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: You need the participle concerned, with -ed, after I'm.
Concerning means “about” or “worrying”; the phrase is as far as I'm concerned.
“As far as I'm agree” does not exist; besides, agree does not take be.

glosario.significado: en lo que a mí respecta

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete the expression of partial agreement.
ejercicios.frase: I agree up to a ___, but I still have doubts.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “I agree up to a point, but…” as partial agreement (es: “hasta cierto punto”). The clue is “up to a ___” followed by but, which introduces the reservation. The missing word is point. It is a very useful phrase in debates because it concedes part of the argument before qualifying it.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “hasta cierto punto” is up to a point.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estoy de acuerdo hasta cierto punto, pero sigo teniendo dudas.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Extent forms “to some extent”, but not “up to a extent”; with up to a the word is point.
A calque of Spanish “hasta cierto punto”; the fixed phrase is up to a point, without certain.
“Up to a limit” is not the phrase for partial agreement; we say up to a point.

glosario.definicion_l: the state of being unsure of something · uncertainty about the truth or factuality or existence of something

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete the expression of full agreement.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “I couldn't agree more” as full agreement. The clue is the exclamation and the form couldn't agree: the idea is that it is impossible to agree more. The missing word is more. Although it is negative in form, it expresses complete agreement, which sometimes confuses Spanish speakers.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Complete agreement: I couldn't agree more.

errores_previstos.explicacion: “I couldn't agree less” is not the usual phrase and could be understood as disagreement; full agreement is I couldn't agree more.
“I couldn't agree much” would mean you hardly agree; the phrase uses more.
Better does not form this expression; the comparative used is more.

glosario.significado: no podría estar más de acuerdo

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the most polite way to disagree.
ejercicios.frase: ___ – I think the figures show the opposite.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that in a formal debate disagreement is softened, and the table includes “I'm afraid I disagree” as polite disagreement. The clue is the instruction, which asks for the most polite form, and the follow-up with arguments (the figures show the opposite). I'm afraid works as a softener, like “me temo” in Spanish.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: I'm afraid I disagree softens the disagreement.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me temo que discrepo; creo que las cifras muestran lo contrario.

Correct. I'm afraid softens the disagreement and makes it polite, as the card recommends.
Incorrect. It is grammatically correct, but it sounds abrupt and blunt; the card advises avoiding it in a formal debate.
Incorrect. It is offensive; it is never a polite way to disagree.

glosario.definicion_l: a diagram or picture illustrating textual material · alternative names for the body of a human being

ejercicios.frase: How do you ___ about the new timetable?
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “How do you feel about…?” (es: “¿qué te parece…?”) as a way of asking for an opinion. The clue is How at the beginning: with think the question is formed with what (What do you think about…?), not with how. That is why only feel works here. Agree cannot be used to ask for an opinion.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: How do you feel about…? asks for an opinion; with think it would be What do you think about…?

por_opcion.feel: Correct. How do you feel about…? asks for someone's opinion or impression.
por_opcion.think: Incorrect. With think the question is What do you think about…?; “How do you think about” is not used.
por_opcion.agree: Incorrect. Agree means “to share an opinion” and does not form an opinion question with how … about.

glosario.definicion_l: a schedule listing events and the times at which they will take place · a schedule of times of arrivals and departures

ejercicios.frase: My parents ___ about money all the time; it's very stressful.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card makes clear that discuss means “to debate, to talk about a subject” and that Spanish “discutir” in the sense of quarrelling is argue. The clue is “it's very stressful”: it is not a calm debate but a quarrel. Also, argue about is the natural combination; discuss does not take about.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mis padres discuten por dinero todo el tiempo; es muy estresante.

por_opcion.argue: Correct. Argue means “to quarrel”, which fits with it being stressful.
por_opcion.discuss: Incorrect. Discuss means “to talk about a subject, to debate” and does not take about; it is the false friend of Spanish “discutir”.
por_opcion.debate: Incorrect. Debate is a formal exchange of arguments, not a stressful family quarrel.

glosario.definicion_l: present reasons and arguments · have an argument about something

ejercicios.frase: It won't destroy jobs. ___, it will create thousands.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that on the contrary rejects what has been said, while on the other hand contrasts two of your own ideas. The clue is the first, negative sentence, “It won't destroy jobs”, followed by the opposite statement. That is why the option is On the contrary. However introduces a contrast, but not the idea of “exactly the opposite”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To counter by stating the opposite: on the contrary.
ejercicios.traduccion: No destruirá empleo. Al contrario, creará miles de puestos.

por_opcion.On the contrary: Correct. On the contrary denies what came before and states the opposite: it will not destroy jobs, it will create them.
por_opcion.On the other hand: Incorrect. On the other hand presents another aspect of the issue; it does not reject what has been said.
por_opcion.However: Incorrect. However signals a contrast or a concession, not the statement of the opposite.

ejercicios.frase: I am not agree with the new rules.
respuestas: I don't agree with the new rules.
I do not agree with the new rules.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card insists that agree is a verb and does not take be: I agree, not “I am agree”. The clue is “I am not agree”, a calque of Spanish “no estoy de acuerdo”. As it is an ordinary verb, the negative is formed with don't: “I don't agree with the new rules”. The uncontracted form “I do not agree” is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Agree is a verb: the negative is formed with don't.
ejercicios.traduccion: No estoy de acuerdo con las nuevas normas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I am not agree with the new rules.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: agree is a verb and does not take be.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I not agree with the new rules.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The negative of an ordinary verb needs the auxiliary do: I don't agree.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I don't agree the new rules.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition is missing: you agree with something.

glosario.definicion_l: be in accord; be in agreement · consent or assent to a condition, or agree to do something
a principle or condition that customarily governs behavior · something regarded as a normative example

ejercicios.frase: Tomorrow we will discuss about the budget.
respuestas: Tomorrow we will discuss the budget.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card states that discuss means “to debate” and takes no about: discuss a topic. The clue is “discuss about”, a calque of Spanish “discutir sobre”. Discuss is transitive and takes the topic directly after it. The correction is “we will discuss the budget” (or we'll discuss).

errores_previstos.respuesta: Tomorrow we will discuss about the budget.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: discuss does not take about.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Tomorrow we will argue the budget.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Argue means “to quarrel” or “to put forward an argument”; to deal with a topic in a meeting we use discuss.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Tomorrow we will discuss on the budget.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Discuss takes no preposition at all: discuss the budget.

glosario.definicion_l: to consider or examine in speech or writing · speak with others about (something); talk (something) over in detail; have a discussion
a sum of money allocated for a particular purpose · a summary of intended expenditures along with proposals for how to meet them

ejercicios.frase: According to me, the reform is necessary.
respuestas: In my opinion, the reform is necessary.
In my view, the reform is necessary.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's typical mistakes explain that according to is used for other sources (according to the report), not for yourself. The clue is “According to me”, a calque of Spanish “según yo”. The correction is “In my opinion” or “In my view”, phrases from the table for giving your own opinion.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: According to is not used for your own opinion.
ejercicios.traduccion: En mi opinión, la reforma es necesaria.

errores_previstos.respuesta: According to me, the reform is necessary.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: according to is not used with the first person.

errores_previstos.respuesta: In my opinion, the reform is necessary according to me.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It adds the correct phrase but keeps according to me, which is still wrong.

errores_previstos.respuesta: On my opinion, the reform is necessary.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition in the phrase is in: in my opinion.

ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “I see what you mean, but…” as partial agreement. Here see means “understand”, and what you mean is an indirect question, so the subject you goes before the verb mean, with no inversion. The order is I + see + what + you + mean.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Understanding someone's point: I see what you mean.

errores_previstos.explicacion: In an indirect question the subject goes before the verb: what you mean.
Putting the object first is not the natural order; the sentence starts with the subject: I see what you mean.

ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “What's your view on…?” as a formal way of asking for an opinion. The order is What's (what is), the possessive your, the noun view and the preposition on with the topic, this. View on means “position on”; note that the preposition is on, not about or of.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Asking for an opinion formally: What's your view on…?

errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition on goes after view: your view on this.
The possessive your goes with view, and the topic, this, goes after on.

ejercicios.frase: After a long meeting, we finally agreed ___ a date for the trip.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card distinguishes agree with someone, agree on a decision and agree to a proposal. The clue is “a date for the trip”: it is a decision the group makes together, so the preposition is on. The result is “we finally agreed on a date”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Reaching agreement on something is agree on.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tras una larga reunión, por fin nos pusimos de acuerdo en una fecha para el viaje.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Agree with is used with people or ideas; for a joint decision we say agree on.
Agree to means accepting someone else's proposal; several people reaching agreement on something is agree on.
A calque of Spanish “ponerse de acuerdo en”: the preposition is on.

glosario.definicion_l: a journey for some purpose (usually including the return) · a hallucinatory experience induced by drugs

ejercicios.frase: It ___ to me that the problem is lack of time, not money.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “It seems to me that…” (es: “me parece que”). The clue is the structure “It ___ to me that”: the impersonal subject it with seem and to me. Think is not built with it or with to me, and look would require like or as if.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “me parece que” is it seems to me that.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me parece que el problema es la falta de tiempo, no de dinero.

por_opcion.seems: Correct. It seems to me that is the phrase for Spanish “me parece que”.
por_opcion.thinks: Incorrect. Think needs a personal subject (I think that…); “it thinks to me” does not exist.
por_opcion.looks: Incorrect. Look in this sense goes with like or as if (“It looks like…”), not with to me that.

descripcion_larga_es: This card brings together the expressions for giving your opinion, asking for other people's, showing full or partial agreement and disagreeing without sounding abrupt: in my opinion, as far as I'm concerned, I couldn't agree more, I'm afraid I disagree. They are the basis of any debate or oral presentation. Spanish speakers find them difficult because agree is a verb (not “I am agree”), discuss does not mean “to quarrel” and according to cannot be used for your own opinion.

contexto.que_es: It is the repertoire of phrases for expressing and asking for opinions, showing agreement and disagreement with different degrees of intensity and politeness, and countering or qualifying arguments. It also includes the prepositions used with agree (with, on, to) and the difference between discuss and argue.
contexto.por_que_importa: Giving opinions and debating is one of the central tasks of any oral exam and of work meetings. In English direct disagreement (You're wrong) sounds aggressive, so knowing softened phrases is as important as grammar. Mistakes like “I am agree” or “according to me” are noticed immediately.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: They are used in debates, interviews, meetings and presentations where you have to take a position. The signals are questions like What do you think about…? or statements you have to react to. Spanish speakers tend to copy “estoy de acuerdo” with be, “discutir sobre” with discuss about and “según yo” with according to.
